Start fresh or build from a template
Join a public circle
Choose a public circle and tap Join.
Public circles appear in the list. This sample does not join a real circle.
Join with a code
Tap Join with code for an invite-only circle.
Ask the circle owner for its invite code. Joining and creating may have limits shown on the real screen.
Enter the invite code
Enter the six-character code, then tap Join.
The code shown here is a sample. No join request is sent during practice.
Open your circle
Tap a circle you have joined to see its members.
Your joined circles appear in your circle list. Open one to see members, ranks, and live focus status.
Create a circle
Tap Create Circle to start your own group.
The real screen shows whether you can create a circle. You may need a check-in streak first. Practice creates nothing.
Choose who can join
Name your circle and choose Public or Private.
Public circles can be discovered by others. Private circles use an invite code from the circle details. Then tap Create when you are ready.
Meet your circle
See members and their focus ranks here.
Member rows show focus time and rank. Connection requests may need Premium and acceptance. Practice sends no requests.
Study together
Select your circle in Ekagra, then start focusing.
A live badge appears while a member is focusing. Joining a circle alone does not start a timer. All focus time here is sample data.
Choose your mood
Tap the mood that matches how you feel.
A check-in records how you feel today. This practice does not save a mood or change your streak.
Add a little detail
Adjust the intensity and add an optional reason or note.
The slider shows how strongly you feel it. Reasons and notes can help you understand your moods later.
Save your check-in
Tap Save Check-in when you are ready.
Choose a mood first. The real save button records your check-in; Next only shows a local example here.
Review past check-ins
Use History to look back at your moods.
History shows recent check-ins with their intensity, notes, and date. This entry is a sample.
Start with a thought
Choose a prompt or tap Write to begin.
Swipe the prompts for ideas. You can answer one or write your own entry without a prompt.
Write your entry
Add a title and your thoughts, then tap Save Entry.
The title is optional. Write a few lines about your day. This practice does not save or publish anything.
Read your journal
Tap View All, then open an entry to read it.
Saved entries appear in your journal list. This sample entry is kept only in the tutorial.
See your streaks
Check your daily check-in and login streaks.
Streaks count consecutive days of activity. A restore option appears only when the app says you are eligible.
See active days
Use the calendar to spot days you were active.
Marked dates come from your login history. The days shown here are samples.
See your consistency
Use the trend chart to review completed goals.
The chart summarizes the last seven days. It helps you see your routine without changing any goals.
Start with an overview
Use Overview to see your progress in one place.
The section buttons lead to Goals, Ekagra, Kavach, and Monthly Review. These summaries use sample data in practice.
Review your goals
Open Goals to compare planned and completed work.
Goal counts, completion trends, and study time help you review your routine. They do not edit your goals.
Review focus time
Open Ekagra to see recorded focus sessions and time.
Focus summaries come from your saved Ekagra sessions. Practice does not start or save a session.
Review a month
Open Monthly Review and choose a month.
Use the month controls to compare reports and achievements. Practice does not generate a real report.
Plan: choose an exam
Use New Plan to create an exam plan, or open a saved one.
This tab holds your exam plans. A saved plan has an overflow menu for its main actions. The tutorial uses a sample plan and skips detailed setup.
Home: your daily work
Check today’s topics, Daily To-do, and the add buttons.
Use Today and Done to switch lists. Mark completed work or add a topic from your syllabus. The settings menu controls your plan. Practice changes nothing.
Syllabus: organize topics
Open a subject to see chapters and topics.
Use the add and overflow buttons to manage your syllabus. The date and plan controls are at the top. This is a short overview, not a setup lesson.
Calendar: see your schedule
Choose a day to see its topics and revisions.
Month arrows move through the calendar. A day opens its study log; scheduling controls help with unfinished work. No dates are changed in practice.
Progress: review your plan
Check completion, your study pace, and the exam countdown.
This tab summarizes progress, subject coverage, revisions, and recorded study time. Use it to see how your plan is going; it does not require entering new data.
